absent: Locking, reference counting and concurrency rules for mount, queue, neighbour and FAT objects.
System call numbers, entry addresses and kernel side handler behavior for tree, mount, file system, statmount, message queue and neighbour operations.
Neighbour reachability transition triggers, timers and netlink sequencing beyond flag and state values.
FAT allocation, validation and error recovery behavior beyond on disk layout constants.
Time, credential and namespace semantics for mount identifiers, attributes and queue permissions.

findings.text: MS_SUBMOUNT MS_NOREMOTELOCK MS_NOSEC MS_BORN MS_ACTIVE and MS_NOUSER occupy successive high bits twenty six through thirty one of a thirty two bit mount flag word, marking submount state, remote lock exemption, security exemption, born completion, active attachment and user prohibition respectively.

MS_RMT_MASK combines read only, synchronous, mandatory lock, version and lazy time behaviors for remount propagation, while MS_MGC_VAL and MS_MGC_MSK expose a fixed historic magic pattern and its high half mask for mount argument validation.

OPEN_TREE_CLONE and OPEN_TREE_NAMESPACE occupy bits zero and one for cloning and new namespace creation with OPEN_TREE_CLOEXEC aliasing close on exec behavior, MOVE_MOUNT_F_SYMLINKS MOVE_MOUNT_F_AUTOMOUNTS and MOVE_MOUNT_F_EMPTY_PATH use values one two and four on the source side while MOVE_MOUNT_T_SYMLINKS MOVE_MOUNT_T_AUTOMOUNTS and MOVE_MOUNT_T_EMPTY_PATH use sixteen thirty two and sixty four on the destination side with MOVE_MOUNT_SET_GROUP at two hundred fifty six MOVE_MOUNT_BENEATH at five hundred twelve and MOVE_MOUNT__MASK aggregating permitted bits, FSOPEN_CLOEXEC is one, FSPICK_CLOEXEC FSPICK_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW FSPICK_NO_AUTOMOUNT and FSPICK_EMPTY_PATH are one two four and eight, and FSMOUNT_CLOEXEC and FSMOUNT_NAMESPACE are one and two.

fsconfig_command orders nine actions zero through eight as flag, string, binary, path, empty path, descriptor, creation or reuse, reconfiguration and exclusive creation, while MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY MOUNT_ATTR_NOSUID MOUNT_ATTR_NODEV and MOUNT_ATTR_NOEXEC occupy the lowest four bits, MOUNT_ATTR__ATIME defines a multi bit atime mode with MOUNT_ATTR_RELATIME MOUNT_ATTR_NOATIME MOUNT_ATTR_STRICTATIME and MOUNT_ATTR_NODIRATIME variants, and MOUNT_ATTR_IDMAP and MOUNT_ATTR_NOSYMFOLLOW occupy widely separated higher bits for identity mapping and symlink prohibition.
mount_attr is a thirty two byte record of four eight byte unsigned fields in order attr_set, attr_clr, propagation and userns_fd, with MOUNT_ATTR_SIZE_VER0 fixing version zero length at thirty two.

statmount header orders size, mnt_opts, mask, sb_dev_major, sb_dev_minor, sb_magic, sb_flags, fs_type, mnt_id, mnt_parent_id, mnt_id_old, mnt_parent_id_old, mnt_attr and mnt_propagation, where size gives total length, mask reports populated groups, device and magic identify the superblock, identifiers distinguish mount parent and legacy views with root self parentage, and attribute and propagation words carry mount option state.

statmount tail orders mnt_peer_group, mnt_master, propagate_from, mnt_root, mnt_point, mnt_ns_id, fs_subtype, sb_source, opt_num, opt_array, opt_sec_num, opt_sec_array, supported_mask, mnt_uidmap_num, mnt_uidmap, mnt_gidmap_num, mnt_gidmap, spare array and str, where numeric offsets address strings inside the trailing variable area and counts size the option and identifier map arrays.

mnt_id_req orders size, a shared word usable as mnt_ns_fd or mnt_fd, mnt_id, param and mnt_ns_id, with MNT_ID_REQ_SIZE_VER0 at twenty four bytes covering through param and MNT_ID_REQ_SIZE_VER1 at thirty two bytes adding the namespace identifier.

STATMOUNT_SB_BASIC STATMOUNT_MNT_BASIC STATMOUNT_PROPAGATE_FROM STATMOUNT_MNT_ROOT STATMOUNT_MNT_POINT STATMOUNT_FS_TYPE STATMOUNT_MNT_NS_ID STATMOUNT_MNT_OPTS STATMOUNT_FS_SUBTYPE STATMOUNT_SB_SOURCE STATMOUNT_OPT_ARRAY STATMOUNT_OPT_SEC_ARRAY STATMOUNT_SUPPORTED_MASK STATMOUNT_MNT_UIDMAP and STATMOUNT_MNT_GIDMAP select single bit groups from the lowest bit upward, LSMT_ROOT uses all ones for the root, LISTMOUNT_REVERSE uses bit zero for reverse order, and STATMOUNT_BY_FD uses value one for descriptor lookup.

mq_attr orders mq_flags, mq_maxmsg, mq_msgsize, mq_curmsgs and four reserved longs, where flags control behavior, maxima bound count and size, current count reports occupancy, and reserved slots are ignored on input and cleared on output.

MQ_PRIO_MAX fixes maximum priority at thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight, MQ_BYTES_MAX fixes maximum bytes at eight hundred nineteen thousand two hundred, NOTIFY_NONE NOTIFY_WOKENUP and NOTIFY_REMOVED map to zero one and two, and NOTIFY_COOKIE_LEN fixes cookie length at thirty two.

SECTOR_SIZE fixes five hundred twelve bytes with SECTOR_BITS nine and MSDOS_DIR_BITS five, MSDOS_DPS and MSDOS_DPB derive entries per sector and block with MSDOS_DPB_BITS and MSDOS_DPS_BITS four, MSDOS_LONGNAME caps at two hundred fifty six, MSDOS_ROOT_INO and MSDOS_FSINFO_INO fix one and two, and FAT_LFN_LEN MSDOS_NAME and MSDOS_SLOTS fix two hundred fifty five, eleven and twenty one.

ATTR_NONE ATTR_RO ATTR_HIDDEN ATTR_SYS ATTR_VOLUME ATTR_DIR and ATTR_ARCH map to zero one two four eight sixteen and thirty two, ATTR_UNUSED combines volume archive system and hidden, ATTR_EXT combines read only hidden system and volume, CASE_LOWER_BASE and CASE_LOWER_EXT use eight and sixteen, DELETED_FLAG uses hex E five with IS_FREE treating empty or that marker as free, and MSDOS_DOT and MSDOS_DOTDOT pad dot names to full short width.

FAT_START_ENT starts cluster numbering at two, MAX_FAT12 MAX_FAT16 and MAX_FAT32 cap usable clusters per width, BAD_FAT12 BAD_FAT16 and BAD_FAT32 mark defective clusters, EOF_FAT12 EOF_FAT16 and EOF_FAT32 terminate chains, FAT_ENT_FREE FAT_ENT_BAD and FAT_ENT_EOF alias zero and the thirty two bit bad and end values, FAT_FSINFO_SIG1 and FAT_FSINFO_SIG2 fix the two signatures checked by IS_FSINFO, and FAT_STATE_DIRTY uses one.

CF_LE_W CF_LE_L CT_LE_W and CT_LE_L convert sixteen and thirty two bit quantities between processor and little endian disk order in both directions, FAT_MAX_DIR_ENTRIES fixes sixty five thousand five hundred thirty six with FAT_MAX_DIR_SIZE derived by entry size shift, and IS_FSINFO requires both signatures to match after conversion.
Directory listing entry orders d_ino, d_off, d_reclen and d_name, where inode and offset locate the entry, record length sizes it, and name provides a two hundred fifty six byte buffer.

Control operations VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_BOTH VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_SHORT FAT_IOCTL_GET_ATTRIBUTES FAT_IOCTL_SET_ATTRIBUTES and FAT_IOCTL_GET_VOLUME_ID share one magic value with distinct numbers for dual name reading, short name reading, attribute query, attribute update and volume query, using read direction for queries and write direction for updates with paired entries or thirty two bit payloads.

fat_boot_sector orders jump bytes, system identifier, sector size, sectors per cluster, reserved count, fat count, directory entry count, sector count, media code, fat length, track geometry, hidden and total sector counts, then a variant tail where the sixteen bit form holds drive, state, signature, volume identifier, label and type while the thirty two bit form adds fat length, flags, version, root cluster, information sector, backup sector and reserved words before the same drive label group.

fat_boot_fsinfo orders first signature, a large reserved run, second signature, free cluster count with minus one meaning unknown, next allocation hint and trailing reserved words, msdos_dir_entry orders short name, attribute, case, creation centiseconds, creation time, creation date, access date, high start, time, date, low start and size, and msdos_dir_slot orders sequence identifier, three name fragments, attribute, reserved byte, checksum and zero start cluster.

MSG_STAT MSG_INFO and MSG_STAT_ANY use eleven twelve and thirteen for status, information and any queue status, MSG_NOERROR MSG_EXCEPT and MSG_COPY use octal flag bits for oversize tolerance, exception reception and non destructive copy, and MSGMNI MSGMAX and MSGMNB fix thirty two thousand identifiers, eight thousand one hundred ninety two byte messages and sixteen thousand three hundred eighty four default queue bytes.

MSGPOOL derives kilobytes from identifier count times queue bytes, MSGTQL and MSGMAP reuse queue byte count for header and map sizes, MSGSSZ fixes sixteen byte segments, __MSGSEG divides pool bytes by segment size, and MSGSEG caps the result at sixty five thousand five hundred thirty five.

msqid_ds orders permission block, two unused queue link pointers, send receive and change times, two reuse words for thirty two bit compatibility, current bytes, message count and byte limit, and last sender and receiver process identifiers, msgbuf pairs a long type with a one byte text placeholder for a variable tail, and msginfo orders pool, map, maximum size, queue bytes, identifier count, segment size, header count and segment count.

ndmsg orders family, padding, interface index, state, flags and type, while attributes NDA_UNSPEC NDA_DST NDA_LLADDR NDA_CACHEINFO NDA_PROBES NDA_VLAN NDA_PORT NDA_VNI NDA_IFINDEX NDA_MASTER NDA_LINK_NETNSID NDA_SRC_VNI NDA_PROTOCOL NDA_NH_ID NDA_FDB_EXT_ATTRS NDA_FLAGS_EXT NDA_NDM_STATE_MASK and NDA_NDM_FLAGS_MASK run from zero upward with NDA_MAX one below the sentinel.

NTF_USE NTF_SELF NTF_MASTER NTF_PROXY NTF_EXT_LEARNED NTF_OFFLOADED NTF_STICKY and NTF_ROUTER occupy successive low bits zero through seven, while NTF_EXT_MANAGED NTF_EXT_LOCKED and NTF_EXT_EXT_VALIDATED occupy the lowest three bits of a separate extended byte.

NUD_INCOMPLETE NUD_REACHABLE NUD_STALE NUD_DELAY NUD_PROBE and NUD_FAILED use successive single bit values one through thirty two for the resolution lifecycle, with NUD_NONE zero and NUD_NOARP and NUD_PERMANENT at the top bits for static exemptions.

nda_cacheinfo orders confirmation, use, update and reference count as thirty two bit values, ndt_stats orders eleven sixty four bit counters for allocations, destroys, hash growth, failures, lookups, hits, probe receptions, collections and full events, ndtmsg carries family plus padding, and ndt_config orders key length, entry size, entry count, flush age, random age, hash seed, mask, chain collection threshold and proxy queue length.

Table parameters from interface and timing controls through queue, probe, delay, lock and interval controls run from zero upward with NDTPA_MAX one below the sentinel, table attributes from name and thresholds through configuration, parameter nesting, statistics, interval and pad run likewise with NDTA_MAX derived the same way, forwarding database notification uses the lowest two bits for activity and inactivity, and NFEA_UNSPEC NFEA_ACTIVITY_NOTIFY and NFEA_DONT_REFRESH run from zero with NFEA_MAX one below the sentinel.
Guards _LINUX_MQUEUE_H _UAPI_LINUX_MSDOS_FS_H _UAPI_LINUX_MSG_H _UAPI__LINUX_NEIGHBOUR_H and _UAPI_LINUX_NET_H each prevent repeated inclusion of their respective user visible header.

Callers must validate statmount size and string offsets against total length before dereference, select mnt_ns_fd versus mnt_fd from mnt_id_req based on negotiated size, update MOUNT_ATTR__ATIME modes with masking rather than whole word overwrite, and treat msg_first, msg_last and reserved words as non portable.

MOUNT_ATTR_SIZE_VER0 fixes thirty two, MNT_ID_REQ_SIZE_VER0 and MNT_ID_REQ_SIZE_VER1 fix twenty four and thirty two, NDA_MAX NDTPA_MAX NDTA_MAX and NFEA_MAX equal sentinel minus one, and MSGSEG caps derived segments at sixty five thousand five hundred thirty five.
